name: Calder & Murn Houndstooth Sport Coat
description:
Calder & Murn is a mid-tier tailoring house out of Milwaukee's Tier 3 professional corridor, known for doing traditional men's and women's suiting without the corponation markup. The Houndstooth Sport Coat is their most recognizable piece — a structured single-button jacket in a cream-and-charcoal houndstooth pattern woven from a wool-viscose blend that holds its shape through a long transit commute. The lapels are notched and moderate, the chest pocket is functional, the interior has two slip pockets and one with a button flap. Lining is a deep burgundy microweave that catches the light when the jacket opens.

This is the jacket a mid-level project manager wears to a client meeting when they want to look put-together without looking corporate. It reads as thoughtful rather than flashy — someone who chose this deliberately. The cut is relaxed enough that it doesn't feel like armor. You see it at Tier 3 restaurants, at gallery openings in the transit district, at university faculty events. It's not trying to signal anything except that you know what you're doing.
what_it_says: You have taste, you have enough money to exercise it, and you didn't need a logo to prove either.
story_hooks: A Calder & Murn sport coat turns up in a Tier 1 pawn shop — the interior button-flap pocket has a folded note inside that shouldn't exist.
Calder & Murn is quietly being acquired by a corponation that plans to gut the workshop and replace production with automated fabrication — the last human-sewn run is already being made.
Someone is wearing this jacket at every single meeting before a string of Tier 3 contract murders; witnesses remember the houndstooth but nothing else.
